findings.evidence: template/scripts/machine_pool.py:350-356 creates the queue with mode 0777 and chmods an owned existing queue to 0777. Under a group-writable, setgid pool directory with mode 02775, non-group accounts can traverse the parent and delete live queue tickets or insert stray entries. _acquire fails when its ticket disappears, and _ticket_order at lines 363-366 rejects stray entries, so these actions can stop participating runs. docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md presents shared-group setup separately from world-writable setup for machines where every account is trusted.
findings.summary: The queue becomes world-writable even when the operator chooses the documented shared-group setup, allowing unrelated local accounts to disrupt validation.
